key_insight: The biggest miss was failing to predict the fp16 scope expansion request. The PR title/description focused on bfloat16 groupwise support, but a maintainer naturally asked 'what about fp16 too?' This is a common review pattern: when you add support for one dtype, reviewers will ask about adjacent dtypes. The triage was wrong because this required a revision cycle — not ready_to_merge as predicted.
hypothesis: I over-indexed on the PR being small and well-tested, which made me predict 'ready_to_merge' with minimal friction. I should have recognized a common review pattern: when a PR adds support for one dtype variant (bf16), reviewers often ask about the neighboring variant (fp16). The PR description even mentioned fp16 channelwise in its 'Purpose' section but the code only handled bf16 groupwise — this gap should have been a signal. A useful skill to develop: 'dtype completeness check' — when a PR adds dtype-specific handling, flag whether all relevant dtypes in the same family are covered, because reviewers will ask. Additionally, I wasted a prediction on latency overhead concerns that no domain expert would raise for a simple upcast — I should trust that kernel developers already know the performance characteristics of dtype conversions.
